# Isaiah Chapter 43 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 155v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_043_page_001.jpg

---

**43:1** But-now [ve-attah] thus says YHWH, your-Creator [borakha], O-Yaakov, and-your-Former [veyotsrekha], O-Yisra'el: "Do-not fear [al-tira], for I-have-redeemed-you [ge'altikha]; I-have-called [qarati] [you] by-your-name [be-shimkha] — you [are] mine [li-atta]."

**43:2** "When you-pass [ta'avor] through-the-waters [ba-mayim], I [will be] with-you [ittekha]; and-through the-rivers [u-va-neharot], they-will-not overflow-you [lo yishtefukha]; when you-walk [telekh] through-fire [be-mo-esh], you-will-not be-burned [lo tikkaveh], and-flame [lehavah] will-not consume-you [lo tiv'ar bakh]."

**43:18** "Do-not remember [al-tizkeru] the-former-things [ri'shonot], and-the-ancient-things [qadmoniyyot] do-not consider [al-titbonanu]."

**43:19** "Behold, I [am] doing [oseh] a-new-thing [chadashah]; now [attah] it-springs-forth [titsmach] — do-you-not perceive-it [halo tede'uha]? Indeed [af] I-will-make [asim] in-the-wilderness [ba-midbar] a-way [derekh], in-the-desert [bi-yeshimon] rivers [neharot]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "I have called you by name":** The intimacy of YHWH's relationship with Israel — not a generic "my people" but called *by name*. "You are mine" (*li-attah*) is covenant language at its most personal.

**v.19 — "Behold, I am doing a new thing":** One of the most quoted verses in Isaiah — God's refusal to be confined to past patterns. The "new thing" is the return from exile, described as a second Exodus (water in the wilderness). The command to "forget the former things" is radical: even the Exodus itself is to be eclipsed by what God is about to do.

*— EMET*
